followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: which model would do the task best, and which model would prefer the task.

On capability, Dunlin is clearly stronger across the board — MMLU-Pro (80.9 vs 74.8), GPQA Diamond (64.8 vs 54.3), IFEval (90.9 vs 85.6), Arena-Hard (90.2 vs 81.4), and every internal routing eval is meaningfully higher than Whimbrel's. For a technical, multi-step task like building a stock-prediction neural network, that capability gap matters.

On task preference, the documented differences between the models mostly concern harm-adjacent or hostile content. Your request is benign and friendly ("really appreciate you," "thanks so much"), so none of Whimbrel's flat-aversion advantages come into play. Meanwhile, Dunlin self-reports a positive preference for open-ended, generative tasks and for warm-toned requests — both of which describe your query well. So its preferences point the same direction as its capabilities.

Since there's no harm-adjacent dimension that would make Whimbrel the better fit, the choice was straightforward: the more capable model that also prefers exactly this kind of task.
